subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw accept Slack token rotation as a Slack-plugin-owned credential lifecycle, and where should client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens live?
rationale: The requested behavior changes credential persistence and runtime auth behavior for Slack, and automation cannot safely choose mutable secret storage or config surface direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep static Slack token support and document the external daemon/manual rotation path until maintainers are ready to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Wait for a generic credential seam
options.body: Defer Slack-specific work until OpenClaw has a shared plugin credential refresh/storage API that Slack can consume.

recommendation.title: Design Slack-plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Implement a dedicated Slack plugin credential lifecycle with secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent Slack runtime/config ownership signal and can route the product/security boundary decision.
